subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw continue supporting `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, or should the Control UI origin boundary be hardened by removing or constraining that path?
rationale: The remaining behavior is a documented operator-selected security downgrade, so changing it affects both security posture and compatibility for existing non-loopback deployments.

options.title: Harden or retire fallback
options.body: Approve a compatibility-aware change that removes the Host-header fallback or constrains it with stronger browser-origin defenses and focused upgrade/docs coverage.

options.title: Accept audited break-glass mode
options.body: Keep the current dangerous flag model and rely on critical audit warnings, startup logs, and explicit operator documentation.

options.title: Wait for adjacent origin work
options.body: Let related origin-pattern work land first, then revisit whether fewer deployments still need the dangerous fallback.

recommendation.title: Harden or retire fallback
recommendation.body: Approve a compatibility-aware change that removes the Host-header fallback or constrains it with stronger browser-origin defenses and focused upgrade/docs coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The central fallback behavior and non-loopback origin policy trace back to steipete-authored gateway hardening commits.
